sections.h2: Ways to turn a Hendersonville house into cash
sections.html:
Three roads lead out. Hire an agent and market the property, find a buyer on your own, or sell to a company that buys homes in whatever condition they are in. The best fit usually comes down to your calendar and how long your repair list is.

  • Agent listing: works for a tidy house and a seller who can keep it show-ready for weeks.
  • Selling it yourself: you set the price and answer the questions, then pass the paperwork to a title company or attorney.
  • Cash buyer: a single offer for the property as it stands today, with a closing date you negotiate.

Hendersonville sits on Old Hickory Lake, around 18 miles northeast of downtown Nashville, and many owners here are weighing a fast exit against a long marketing period.

sections.h2: Lake, roads and what buyers ask
sections.html:
Water shapes this city. Of Hendersonville's 38.18 square miles, about 6.5 are lake and river, so boat docks and shoreline lots show up in local sales. It is the largest city in Sumner County. Lakefront owners should expect questions about flood zones, docks and shoreline rules, so collect any related paperwork early.

Commuters lean on State Route 386 and the parallel U.S. 31E. The typical one-way trip for a Hendersonville worker is 29.7 minutes, so buyers will want to know how far you are from the interstate. Sumner County Schools serve the city, with Hendersonville High, Beech High and Merrol Hyde Magnet among its campuses.

A tornado struck Hendersonville on December 9, 2023. If your house was repaired afterward, keep the permit and inspection papers in one folder for whoever buys it.

The city had 64,266 residents on July 1, 2025, about 4 percent more than at the 2020 base. Most households own, and values are high for Tennessee.

These are citywide middles. Your own price depends on the lot, the updates and the block. The city has 31.42 square miles of land, about 1,966 residents per square mile.

Owners get two bills. The city's bill folds in the annual trash fee and a stormwater charge, so it covers more than property tax alone. The county bill comes from the Sumner County Trustee in Gallatin.

Sumner County reappraises on a five-year cycle. Values were set as of January 1, 2024, and the next round is scheduled for 2029. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value. To question a value, ask the assessor for an informal review before taking it to the county Board of Equalization, which begins its June sessions on the first of the month.

Interest begins March 1 on any balance left unpaid. The trustee's office, at 355 North Belvedere Drive, Room 107, lets you split payment into as many as five check or cash installments. The same office handles state tax relief for older and disabled owners and a tax freeze program covering the county and some cities. Before closing, ask the title company to show how this year's bill is divided.

  • Assessor, informal review: 615-452-2412
  • Trustee: 615-452-1260
  • County appeals: Board of Equalization, June

sections.h2: Closing costs and where the deed goes
sections.html:
Tennessee taxes a transfer at $0.37 per $100 of the price. A mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 applies to new debt, with the first $2,000 exempt. Your sales contract decides who pays what, so read that clause before you sign.

Deeds are filed with the Sumner County Register of Deeds in Gallatin, Suite 201 at 355 N. Belvedere Drive, phone 615-452-3892. The counter opens at 8 a.m. and closes at half past four on weekdays. Most title companies file electronically through Simplifile or CSC ERecording Solutions. Deed books are scanned back to 1786, and records are certified from September 1989.

The office records more than 30,000 documents in a typical fiscal year with a small staff, so allow some lead time when a closing date is tight. MyLandAlert, a free service, emails you whenever a document is recorded under your name, and it is worth turning on around any sale or refinance.

Can a new owner run vacation rentals out of the house? Rarely. City zoning treats any stay under 30 days as a short-term rental, and a 2016 ordinance confines them to Old Town Commercial and General Commercial districts.

Operators in those districts need an engineered site plan, a use and occupancy permit and a business license. An owner who lives in the home and rents out one room does not count, and neither do leases of 30 days or more.

Enforcement starts with a complaint to the police non-emergency line, 615-451-3838. An inspection follows, then letters from the zoning enforcement officer, and only after that a citation sent to City Court. A buyer planning nightly rentals should call Planning at 615-264-5316 before making an offer.

sections.h2: Permits to sort out before you list
sections.html:
Make a list of any work you paid for that needed a permit: roofing, electrical, plumbing, mechanical or structural. Hendersonville runs these through its Citizen Self-Service portal, where you can apply, upload plans, book inspections and pay fees.

The portal marks each inspection pending, scheduled, passed or failed, and a request must arrive by an afternoon cutoff to be booked for the next business day. The city's main line is 615-822-1000. A buyer paying cash may accept open items, though the offer will reflect them.

sections.h2: From first call to closing day
sections.html:
A smooth sale follows a short script. Start by gathering your tax statements, your lender's payoff contact and permit papers. Then choose a route, and once you have an accepted offer, give the title company everything in one batch. The title company will confirm the payoff, divide the tax bill, prepare the deed and file it with the register.

A financed buyer adds loan approval and an appraisal, either of which can pull a deal back toward repairs or a lower price. A cash buyer skips both, so the date mostly depends on title work. If you need a firm date, ask for it in writing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hendersonville house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. Agents list such houses, owners sell them directly, and cash buyers purchase them as is. Closing out open permits first usually makes the sale smoother, and the offer you receive will reflect repairs that remain.

faqs.q: Who covers the transfer tax at a Hendersonville closing?
faqs.a: Whoever the contract names. The rate is $0.37 per $100 of price, paid when the deed is recorded in Gallatin, and the settlement statement shows the amount.

faqs.q: Which office records a Hendersonville deed?
faqs.a: The Sumner County Register of Deeds, 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Suite 201, Gallatin, 615-452-3892. Title companies normally submit electronically.

faqs.q: When is the next Sumner County reappraisal?
faqs.a: 2029. The most recent round reflected values as of January 1, 2024, and yearly appeals go to the county Board of Equalization beginning June 1.

faqs.q: Are weekend rentals allowed in Hendersonville?
faqs.a: Only in Old Town Commercial and General Commercial zones, with a site plan, use and occupancy permit and business license. Rentals of 30 days or longer fall outside the short-term rule.
